Attachments: compute_scenarios_v2.xlsx (model with assumptions)

Asks (deliver by end of day Tue 5/18):

- Karthik: list constraints on slot bursting and any SLO implications for 2x burst or >20% slot increase.
- Irene & Lauren: pick two leadership scenarios (Conservative / Aggressive) and the narrative bullets we’ll use to justify each.

Please keep bullets short and call out whether numbers include batching/cache benefits or not. If you add rows/assumptions to the sheet, flag them with comments.

Thanks — short sync if needed tomorrow 10am PT.

—Dylan

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: QBR — capacity scenarios, GPU spend, utilization, batching & cache impacts

Attaching a quick export from the modeling run: slot_run_rates.csv. I've also updated compute_scenarios_v2.xlsx with the following notes.

Highlights — baseline (no extra batching/cache levers):
- Current sustained utilization: 64% (weighted across gen+embed fleets).
- Forecast H2 demand growth (median): +28% QoQ across hosted API traffic.
- GPU unit cost (effective after reserved commitments): $0.73/token-equivalent per 10k tokens (see sheet).

Estimated impact of common levers (workload mix: 45% chat, 40% single-turn generation, 15% embeddings):
- Continuous batching (better packing across short sequences): ~7–11% cost reduction vs baseline at 95th percentile latency target.
- KV/prefix caching for chat: additional 12–18% token-cost savings for chat-heavy routes; overall platform-level effect ≈ 4–6%.
- Aggressive quantization (Q4 roadmap, not in current model): potential 15–20% further reduction but affects per-request inference quality — flag for Product.

Assumptions called out in the sheet. If anyone wants the scenario run with alternate latency SLOs, say so; I can rerun.

Attachments: slot_run_rates.csv

—Marissa
Senior Product Ops, Infra Economics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: QBR — capacity scenarios, GPU spend, utilization, batching & cache impacts

Quick ops constraints and risk notes:

- Slot bursting: the stack currently allows short bursts to ~25% above baseline, but sustained >20% burst risks eviction behavior on shared nodes and increases tail latency risk for latency-sensitive customers.
- Autoscaling cooldowns: 90s default; for very spiky traffic (customer-facing chat), this means batching gains can be diminished if autoscaling can't keep up — we should show a scenario with 30s cooldown (experimental) vs default.
- KV cache TTL changes: increasing TTL from 30s→120s gives good prefix hit rates for repeat-turn dialogs but increases memory pressure on the serving pool; providing an explicit memory-limited cache (per-tenant caps) should be included as mitigation.

I'll add a short appendix to the model (kv_cache_sensitivity.pdf) showing memory vs hit-rate curves.

—Karthik
VP, Serving Orchestration

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: QBR — capacity scenarios, GPU spend, utilization, batching & cache impacts

Thanks — this is shaping up. Leadership framing suggestion for the deck:

1) Conservative scenario (recommended baseline):
- Show current commitments + modest demand growth (+15% vs baseline in model)
- Emphasize reliability-first actions: tighten autoscale cooldowns only after validation, prefer incremental KV TTL increases with per-tenant memory caps
- Expected impact on unit cost: ~6–8% improvement (batching + controlled caching)

2) Aggressive scenario (opportunity play):
- Assume prioritized engineering work (30s cooldowns, experimental burst slots up to +30% for scheduled events, and platform-wide prefix caching + per-tenant caps)
- Include optional aggressive quantization as a separate toggle
- Expected impact: ~18–25% unit-cost improvement over baseline, with clear quality/regression gates

Deck asks: three slides — 1) topline runway (3 scenarios shown), 2) levers & assumptions (bulleted + quick numbers), 3) risk & mitigation (ops constraints + QA gates).

Action: Dylan — assemble slides and pick 2–3 example customer routes (chat, embeddings, long-form gen) to show per-route sensitivity. Marissa — finalize the numbers in the model and send final CSV by 5/20 EOD. Karthik — add the appendix and short ops-runbook notes. Lauren — I defer wording for the exec slide; if you can provide two 1-liners we’ll insert.

Irene
VP, Product & Strategy

Thanks everyone — strong work. Quick decisions and next steps for the deck:

- Use Irene's Conservative / Aggressive framing as primary narrative.
- Include Acme as a short callout "near-term spike example" with two numbers: 3x for 72h (burst plan) and potential prefix-cache benefit (Marissa to quantify in final CSV).
- Slide owners: Dylan (slide 1: runway + scenarios), Marissa (slide 2: numbers & levers), Karthik (slide 3: ops & mitigations).
- Acceptable risk threshold: show Aggressive as "opportunity" with a sideways arrow; do not assume quantization in baseline.

Lauren — can you review the deck draft by Monday 5/24 10am PT? I'll consolidate comments immediately after.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
SVP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
